title: Position- and Momentum-Space Quantum Information Measures of the Double-Morse Oscillator
authors: Firoz Chogle, Ernesto Damiani, Berihu Teklu
abstract: We investigate the quantum-information properties of a particle confined by the double Morse potential in position and momentum spaces. The quasi-exact solvability of the model gives analytical expressions for the first two bound states, allowing the corresponding probability densities to be analyzed directly. Shannon entropy, Onicescu energy, Fisher information, statistical complexity, and Fisher-Shannon products are evaluated as functions of the parameter $A$, which controls the transition from a well-separated double well to a merged single-well profile. The position distribution is more delocalized and structurally complex when the double-well character is pronounced, whereas the momentum distribution exhibits the complementary trend. As the wells merge, the ground-state Fisher--Shannon product approaches its Gaussian reference value, whereas the excited state retains stronger non-Gaussian structure.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the quantum information properties of a particle in the double-Morse potential by calculating metrics like entropy and Fisher information. The research tracks how these measures change as the potential transitions from two separated wells to a single merged well. It demonstrates that the complexity of the position distribution and the uncertainty in the momentum distribution exhibit complementary behaviors across this physical crossover.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum information measures characterize the particle confinement within the double-Morse potential in both position and momentum spaces.
main_result: The position distribution shows increased structural complexity when the double-well character is strong, while the momentum distribution exhibits a complementary trend. The Fisher-Shannon product approaches the Gaussian reference value as the wells merge.
method: The analysis employs various information-theoretic measures—including Shannon entropy, Onicescu energy, and Fisher information—calculated for the first two bound states using quasi-exactly solvable analytical expressions.
model_or_system: The system is the double-Morse oscillator, governed by a potential $V_{DM} = D(A \cosh(\alpha x) - 1)^2$. This model is relevant for systems like ultracold atoms or semiconductor quantum wells.
key_observables: Shannon entropy ($S_ho, S_\gamma$), Onicescu energy ($O_ho, O_\gamma$), Fisher information ($I_ho, I_\gamma$), statistical complexity ($CGL$), and the Fisher-Shannon product ($P$).
important_parameters: The dimensionless shape parameter $A$ controls the crossover from a double-well to a single-well profile, with the analysis focusing on $A \in (0, 1)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is limited to the ground and first excited states due to the quasi-exactly solvable sector used, and the results are interpreted diagnostically rather than as a full device-specific estimation protocol.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the potential $V(y)$ vs. $A$, wavefunctions ($\psi_0, \psi_1$) vs. $A$, energy levels ($\epsilon_0, \epsilon_1$) vs. $A$, and the evolution of various information measures ($S_ho, S_\gamma, O, P, CGL$) as $A$ changes.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the double-Morse potential and its quasi-exact solvability. It then systematically calculates and analyzes several quantum information measures (Shannon, Onicescu, Fisher, etc.) as a function of the parameter $A$, detailing the physical interpretation of the trends observed in the position and momentum domains.
why_interesting: This work provides a quantitative link between the geometry of a confining potential (double-well structure) and the resulting quantum uncertainty and complexity, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum state preparation and measurement in cold atom or superconducting circuit platforms.
